section_4b_pre_print_debates.title: 1. Internal Green Hydrogen Plant Ramp & Fuel Margin Turnaround
section_4b_pre_print_debates.content: Plug Power has historically suffered massive negative gross margins on its hydrogen delivery business due to soaring third-party merchant liquid hydrogen purchase costs. With its 15 TPD Georgia plant operational and Tennessee online, analysts will probe CEO Andy Marsh on whether the internal cost per kilogram is falling below $4/kg and when fuel gross margin turns permanently positive.

section_4b_pre_print_debates.title: 2. DOE $1.66 Billion Loan Facility Closing & Dilution Protection
section_4b_pre_print_debates.content: The U.S. Department of Energy's conditional commitment for up to $1.66 billion in debt financing is the single largest liquidity catalyst in Plug's history. Institutional investors demand concrete timing on definitive documentation closing, conditions precedent, and initial draw schedules to definitively remove the threat of ATM equity offerings.

section_4b_pre_print_debates.title: 3. High Short Float (23.54%) & Commercial Forklift Customer Concentration
section_4b_pre_print_debates.content: With 23.54% of float sold short, Plug Power represents a classic high-beta short squeeze candidate. Bears point to customer concentration in warehouse material handling (Amazon, Walmart, Home Depot) and slow electrolyzer project final investment decisions (FIDs). Any major European or Asian green ammonia electrolyzer contract win could spark a rapid squeeze toward mean PT ($3.39, +142% upside).
